sections.heading: Who I Am
paragraphs: I study Computer Science and Statistics at [UW–Madison|University of Wisconsin–Madison, B.S. in both. Class of 2027.](https://wisc.edu). The statistics half is there because I want to do research, and statistics carries more weight in research than I appreciated going in. Two degrees is slower than one, but I'd rather learn both properly than rush either.

My time splits a few ways right now. I'm a research engineer at Equistamp(https://equistamp.com), working with METR(https://metr.org) and [Redwood Research](https://redwoodresearch.org) on the infrastructure people use to evaluate AI systems: building it, then trying to break it before someone else does. I do a directed study with the [UW Graphics Group](https://graphics.cs.wisc.edu/) on how visualization design guidelines get written, which is a slower and very different kind of careful. And I run [GDG Madison|Google Developer Groups- a developer community!](https://gdg.community.dev/gdg-madison/) as President and lead a technical cohort at [WAISI|Wisconsin AI Safety Initiative](https://waisi.org), where I get to lead a discussion on the technical side of AI safety and help people get their P(Doom) up.

None of that was a plan. I'd rather be confused about something interesting than fluent in something settled, and most of my decisions have followed from that, which is also why the list keeps changing.

items.text: Exploring. Learning things, trying things, following a question well past the point where it's obviously useful. From cooking to games to what I'm working on, I'm constantly looking around for new ideas.

Impact. I want to leave something behind. Even if nobody remembers it was me, I'd like there to be some lasting effect from what I did; whether that comes from something I built, something I found, or the people I knew.
Knowing why. I want to understand how something actually works, not just how to use it. That goes for systems and, honestly, for people too, I like knowing what makes things tick.

Not sitting on it. Knowledge is worth close to nothing held still; we're all here because some caveman told another cavman you could bonk things with rocks. Teaching is also the fastest way I've found to check whether I actually understand something.

sections.heading: How I Got Here
paragraphs: I came into college wanting to study how machines understand and generate language, and assumed I'd end up on a PhD track working on NLP and LLMs. Software engineering was something I was good at and enjoyed but hadn't quite fallen for yet.

Things changed at Meta, and it was less about the work than about how it felt to finish things. I was on the [ENSD|Edge Network Services-Deployment] team on the Infra side, and I kept picking up small projects alongside my main internship project, from something like a like/dislike button on agent responses, right up to a front-facing dashboard that a bunch of teams used to find bottlenecks in company-wide deployments. Finishing something and then watching people use it felt better than any good result I'd gotten on a benchmark. I came out of that summer wanting a lot more of it, and I still do.

AI safety came out of the same instinct, which surprised me. I took the impact-maximizing habit I'd picked up over the summer and started pointing it at everything, and this kept coming back as a place where the gap between how much it matters and how many people work on it is enormous. It was also just interesting, a whole school of thought I'd previously met only through scifi books and movies. An [EAG|EA Global- a conference series for people working on high-impact problems, AI safety among them.] conference is where it went from being a curiosity to a path I wanted to go down.

sections.heading: Marginalia
paragraphs: I have been cooking a lot over the past year, when I moved into an apartment. I default to fried rice in a rush, but love trying out new things. I also enjoy going on hikes whenever I get the chance, and same goes for reading- fiction or otherwise. Planning on turning these into their own corners in the [the Greehouses](/garden/), where I'll talk a bit more about what I'm up to.
[Harry Potter|Click here to read Death of the Author](https://writing.upenn.edu/~taransky/Barthes.pdf) obviously, if you picked up on what I was going for with the theme lol.
I'm also mildly obsessed with oreos, and always have a pack of them within reach around my working area. Same for coffee, though I've been trying to control the caffeine intake off (finals) season.

I fought karate nationally, play basketball, and have spent most of this summer in the gym. I play the guitar and piano too, though not well. Games tend to come and go; right now I'm playing Minecraft and Assassin's Creed Odyssey.

Chess is the one I keep coming back to. I used to compete when I was young, but got back into it in middle school after a few years of hiatus. The higher my elo gets, the more I realize how much room there is to grow above me, which is both annoying and the reason I haven't put it down.
